findings.title: CATALOG_STATES / CATALOG_MORPHS hardcode the BehaviorState and SizeMorph unions without exhaustiveness checking
findings.desc: Scoring uses Record<BehaviorState, number> (compile-time exhaustive), but CATALOG_STATES is merely typed `readonly BehaviorState[]`, so adding a state to BehaviorState (the module docs already anticipate a future SECRET state) compiles cleanly while TOTAL_CATEGORIES stays stale, discoveredEntries silently omits recorded entries of the new state (diverging from categoriesDiscovered), and completionFraction can exceed 1. Same exposure for CATALOG_MORPHS vs SizeMorph; a `satisfies`/exhaustiveness pattern or deriving both lists from one source would close it.

findings.desc: The `distance: number` parameter shadows the module-scope `distance()` imported from vec2.js inside photoScore; harmless today since the body never calls it, but any future edit that does would silently break, and no-shadow lint configs will flag it.

findings.title: demo world spawns player outside bounds
findings.desc: runObservationDemo builds the World with player at (-8, 0) while bounds are [-5, 5]; it works only because the loop overwrites player.position before the first world.step, so any constructor-time validation/clamping or use of the initial position would misbehave.

findings.title: CATALOG_STATES not exhaustively tied to BehaviorState
findings.desc: TOTAL_CATEGORIES, completionFraction, and discoveredEntries all assume CATALOG_STATES covers every BehaviorState, but nothing enforces that (contrast observation.ts's Record<BehaviorState, number>, which would fail compilation); adding a state to the union would silently skew the completion denominator and omit the new categories from discoveredEntries.

findings.title: circular type-only import with sim.ts
findings.desc: snapshot.ts imports Bounds from sim.js while sim.ts imports the snapshot types back; both are `import type` so there is no runtime cycle, but it undercuts the "clean data boundary / decoupling" the module docs emphasize and may trip import-cycle linting — Bounds could live in a shared types module.

findings.title: WELL_FRAMED label inconsistent with framing score at band edges
findings.desc: classifyFraming labels distances exactly 1.5 and 6.0 as WELL_FRAMED (inclusive bounds), but framingQuality's sizing term is exactly 0 at those distances, so a photo displayed as WELL_FRAMED can receive zero framing credit. Additionally the Framing doc says the bucket reflects "how well it fills the shot," but the model is distance-only and ignores subject size, so a LARGE subject at 5.9 and a SMALL subject at 5.9 are bucketed identically.

findings.desc: `categoryOf` determines emptiness from `state` and `phenotype` but never checks `subjectId`. findings.title: Invalid observer FOV/range values are not handled
findings.desc: The public `Observer` API accepts arbitrary numbers, but `creaturesInView` does not validate `fovRadians` or `range`. For example, `NaN` makes both comparisons false and can place every creature in view, while oversized FOV values can include creatures behind the observer despite the cone contract.

findings.title: Catalog is not actually immutable at runtime
findings.desc: `Catalog` exposes a `ReadonlyMap`, but `recordPhoto` stores the caller-provided mutable `Photo` reference directly, and `emptyCatalog`/returned maps are not frozen. A caller can mutate a recorded photo (or cast and mutate the map) and change a prior catalog despite the documentation promising an immutable catalog; copy/freeze stored values or clarify that immutability is only by convention.

findings.title: Food identities are lost at the snapshot boundary
findings.desc: `FoodSnapshot` omits the food patch `id`, even though live-world food specs are identified by ID. Consumers of the advertised renderer/observation boundary therefore cannot distinguish or stably track individual food patches, so this is not a faithful world snapshot.

findings.title: Zero-facing observers can see creatures with a full FOV

findings.title: Missing size range validation
findings.desc: `sizeMorph` does not handle negative or zero size values, which could produce unexpected morph classification if phenotype size is corrupted.

findings.title: Potential floating-point instability
findings.desc: Using `Math.min(1, Math.max(-1, cos))` before `Math.acos` could still produce `NaN` if `la` or `lb` is zero (though earlier check prevents this). Safer to clamp after computing `cos`.

findings.title: Off-axis tie-breaking order may be counter-intuitive
findings.desc: `selectSubject` picks the most centered, then nearer, then lower ID. This means a creature slightly further but same centering will lose to a closer one, which may conflict with visual expectation that a larger distance should be penalized more.

findings.title: Unsafe non-null assertion
findings.desc: `photo.state as BehaviorState` and `photo.phenotype!.size` rely on preceding null check; but `categoryOf` returning non-null doesn't guarantee `photo.phenotype` is non-null (though logically it should). Could use a runtime guard for safety.

findings.title: Hard-coded observer facing logic assumes target at origin
findings.desc: The demo observer faces toward origin `(0,0)`. If the food cluster moves or player starts elsewhere, facing direction may be misaligned with actual subjects, reducing photo quality.

findings.title: Missing explicit weight sum validation
findings.desc: The comment says weights sum to 1.0, but no runtime assertion ensures this; if weights are modified, score could exceed [0,1] range.

findings.desc: `CATALOG_STATES` is a manually-maintained array of literals rather than being derived/enforced against the `BehaviorState` union (unlike `BEHAVIOR_RARITY: Record<BehaviorState, number>` in observation.ts, which the compiler would flag on a new state). If `BehaviorState` ever gains a member not added here, `categoryOf`/`recordPhoto` will still key photos of that state, silently pushing `entries.size` above `TOTAL_CATEGORIES` (breaking the documented `[0,1]` invariant of `completionFraction`) and hiding that category from `discoveredEntries`.

findings.title: Zero-facing "no view" guarantee only holds for FOV < 360°
findings.desc: `angleBetween` returns `Math.PI` for a zero-length facing vector, and `creaturesInView` excludes a creature only when `offAxis > halfFov`. If `fovRadians` is ever configured near/at `2π` (halfFov ≈ π), a zero facing vector would not be excluded, contradicting the documented contract "a zero vector means 'no facing' → nothing is in view." Not triggered by current callers (fixed 90° FOV) but is a latent edge-case bug.

findings.desc: `Photo.subjectId` is the documented indicator that a photo has no subject, but `categoryOf` only checks `state` and `phenotype`; the public `Photo` type permits `subjectId: null` with those fields populated, which would incorrectly create a catalog entry.

findings.title: Catalog is not actually immutable

findings.title: Food identity is lost in snapshots
findings.desc: `FoodSnapshot` omits the live food patch's `id`, unlike `CreatureSnapshot`, preventing renderer/observation consumers from reliably correlating a food patch across snapshots and making the claimed faithful world boundary incomplete.

findings.title: Observer path does not cross the cluster
